description.narrative:
The project "Actions for Inclusive Governance and Accountability: AGIR" is an initiative of the RJNCC to improve the effectiveness of public service for the participation of youth and women in local governance and environmental leadership initiatives. The main objective of this project is to increase the empowerment of youth and women's CSOs in 4 communes in the Tahoua and Maradi regions to ensure that youth and women's voices are represented in policy development or policy reforms, particularly regarding the judicious use of public resources.
The RJNCC will identify eight youth and women's organizations from its network in the two target regions to participate in this project. The RJNCC will empower grassroots organizations working at the intersection of women's and youth rightsto use the data and stories of change from women and youth leaders to build and strengthen community, inspire action and hold poweraccountable. In collaboration with these 8 local organizations, the RJNCC will work to demystify public funding processes for various groups of rights holders by simplifying governance data. This data will be analyzed and transcribed into a creative form through drama for rural people and a mobile platform to centralize all this information for citizens who have internet connected mobile phones. Through this project, the RJNCC aims to stimulate public discourse by supporting women's and youth CSOs with platforms and toolsto take ownership of public space and improve access to public infrastructure. We will strive to build on existing social and valuesystems that can serve as catalysts for action, trust, and a sense of belonging, making it difficult for youth and women in these areas to be ignored in local governance processes. The project aims to: Strengthen the capacity of 8 women and youth CSOs through in-depth training (training of trainers), advocacy toolkits, resources, and tools to effectively engage, analyze, monitor and deepen dialogues with policy makers and governments on public financial management. This includes advocacy, legislative/policy analysis, compliance monitoring, procurement process audits, budget/contract monitoring at local level. Facilitate dialogues between women/youth CSOs and policy makers at the local level: through a peer-to-peer approach with women and youth (from the formal and informal sector)on gender and youth sensitive public procurement issues. Empowering women and youth CSOs through green initiatives: - Through training and coaching on environmental leadership for women - Environmental education for youth to influence the inclusion of the environment and climate change dimension in school curricula in Niger

The Niger Youth Network on Climate Change (RJNCC) is the national representation of African Youth Initiative on Climate Change (AYICC) which is the largest platform for African youth on environmental and climate issues with the African Union and its branches The RJNCC is a group of youth organizations working in the fields of the environment, climate change and renewable energy for Sustainable Development. the Niger Youth Network on Climate Change (RJNCC.AYICC-Niger) is a shared research and training organization which brings together leaders of youth organizations from the Republic of Niger. It essentially establishes interactive links between the various partner structures in order to encourage the dissemination and exchange of information as well asthe development of policies and programs concerning youth, climate change, the environment and sustainable development. . Such a networking space has many advantages such as the synergy of resources, the improvement of the quality of service, informationand scientific communications, better sharing of knowledge and experiences. However, it also poses many questions: What type of organization between partners to set up? What information to disseminate? Which technical supports to choose to communicate? What new uses, what new practices does it bring about? What methods and strategies adopted for the defense and popularization of conventions, treaties and other legislative texts in the field of climate change, the environment and sustainable development?What social and economic reintegration policies to put in place as part of green youth employment? The Niger Youth Network on Climate Change (RJNCC.AYICC-Niger) is a non-governmental, non-profit, apolitical and non-denominational youth information and training organization on youth issues. Its creation, which took place on July 10, 2010, is based on the observation that young people are constantly asked to take part in national development. Hence the need for these young people to be informed and trained to contribute to the best of their abilities. However, the reality today is that young people often ignore important problems for which they could provide solutions. It also appears that the unemployment problem is crucial and is partly due to the lack of professionalism in education on the one hand and the lack of private initiative on the other.
